item.title: 001: Contiguous Memory
item.description: DRAFT 001: Contiguous Memory Motivation Default behaviors, both in systems as well as in people, are incredibly important. The data structures we use day in and day out have a huge impact on performance. While things like asymptotic complexity do have value, I believe the current calculus employed by the average programmer is a bit skewed in the wrong direction. Particularly, I think they are considering things like asymptotic complexity before considering the memory layout of a particular data structure.

item.title: 000: Profiling Cmake Build Times
item.description: DRAFT 000: Optimizing Builds with CMake and Ninja Introduction ¬ Build times should be fast. Live in C++land for long enough and you might forget this, but just look at languages that have prioritized compiler performance, and its clearly viable. Go, Jai and Nim are a couple examples that come to mind. Nim is particularly interesting here because its literally generating C code, giving it to a C compiler and letting it generate the binary.
